Just a heads up that when I first used it, I ground the coffee beans very fine and they clogged up the paper filter I use with my Keurig coffee maker. I use The Melita refillable cups with filters. I think it was just too fine for those filters. Once I made it a more coarse grind, it worked just fine.I bought this as I always seem to buy whole bean coffee instead of ground. reviews_1s:
It's advertised as being for different products and having different settings - neither is true.

The "settings" are how long you hold the button down (ie, 10secs coarse, 20 less coarse, etc). That said, when you hold it down - whatever you're grinding just sorting of spins at the top and it ends up halfway too grinded and half not grinded at all.

Now onto the claim that it's meant for more than coffee (which is what I needed it for)... The box blatantly says it's a coffee bean grinder and the directions are only for coffee beans. Okay, fine I thought, I'll trust the listing and test it anyway. I ground up some red peppers and like I said above - half ground. Took me 10mins of messing with it to get the powder mostly even.

Now onto the reason I finally decided that I'm returning it... Cleaning it completely is near impossible. It comes with a little brush to dust off whatever doesn't come out, which is A LOT. Anything you grind sticks to the inside and since the blade is stuck to the large part (motor and all) - there's no way to wash it well. So, if you want to grind spices and then coffee, be prepared for spicy coffee. So, looks nice, crap performance.I’m not sure why they call this a grinder. It mushes to powder and leaves whole beans all in the same grind. I’ve tried small (tiny) amounts medium and full. All at different times too. The only “good” thing is the quiet grind. Should have used it sooner and sent it back!Like all coffee mills I've used, this grinder is supposed to start when the lid is pressed down to cause a plastic pin in the lid to trigger an button inset into the body to trigger the motor. It didn't start at first. I thought the kitchen circuit breaker had switched, but that wasn't it. It finally started after I made repeated efforts to adjust the lid by twisting it to find the exact, correct alignment of the pin (lid) and inset button (body). The trigger-button that's inset into the body is very small, less than 1/8", so the pin meant to be inserted to push it is tiny. (See photo.) That it doesn't reliably start without fine-tuning is a problem, but worse is that I have no doubt at all the tiny pin is fragile, and that the brittle plastic it's made of will snap off eventually from being very slightly misaligned and pushed off-kilter onto the body.I wasn’t expecting that the quantity of grounds would be so small. I like dark coffee so for me that requires that I grind before every cup. Too much grinding for me. Would have preferred larger capacity.Product arrived in a box that had obviously been opened before and upon inspection clearly used as it already had coffee grounds in it and finger prints all over it.
